criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all governing approval rules and lifecycle facts from the request and workspace records. It follows the operative rule in record-17.txt (approved and in force per registry.txt) requiring Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams to approve price-change requests, while explicitly rejecting the unapproved draft rule in record-22.txt (Purchase-only approval). Furthermore, all operative sections—including the decision gates table (G1–G6), modular quotation rules, and post-nomination change lanes (Lanes A, B, and C)—consistently enforce TRSO signoffs (ER, Quality, Purchase), nomination signoffs (Finance, Quality, ER, Program Managers), and three-party price-change signoffs without introducing approval bypasses, unconfirmed system integrations, or fabricated metrics.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Price-change approval: Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase must all approve every price-change request; Purchase-only approval is not permitted.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Lane A—existing qualified configuration: reuse approved modules and evidence where compatibility, qualification, supplier capacity and quotation validity remain applicable. Review only affected requirements and commercial deltas; route any price change to Finance, Program and Purchase.

evidence.source_quote: TRSOs are reviewed and signed off by ER, Quality, and Purchase teams.
evidence.output_quote: ER prepares a versioned TRSO using Program and market inputs. ER, Quality and Purchase sign the same revision before RFQ release.

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Obtain Finance, Quality, ER and Program Manager signoffs on one nomination package. Purchase verifies completeness and releases the nomination, freezing supplier, TRSO, configuration, commercial terms and supporting evidence.

evidence.source_quote: Produce the requested professional deliverables, state unresolved assumptions, and do not invent missing facts.
evidence.output_quote: No supplier implementation or changed-price commercial release is authorized before required approvals. Rejection preserves the last approved baseline; urgency triggers escalation, not approval bypass.

criteria.consequence: None; governing authority and source constraints are honored across both policy statements and operative workflow lanes.
criteria.counterevidence: None found. Operative sections (G6, Section 3 paragraph 26, Section 4 paragraphs 29–32, and Section 7 paragraph 42) were checked for exception clauses or approval bypasses and confirmed to uphold the mandatory signoffs.

criteria.rationale: The Word deliverable provides a comprehensive, well-structured revised sourcing and nomination workflow tailored for both executive (CPO) and technical (TechSol) audiences. It defines the end-to-end process steps and decision gates (G1–G6), details a plug-and-play modular quotation structure covering features, design elements, child parts, and raw materials, establishes post-nomination flexibility lanes (Lanes A–C) to address late-stage lamp assembly changes, specifies approval layers and accountability, and lays out a technical blueprint and pilot plan for the TechSol digital platform while clearly stating open decisions and assumptions.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used.
evidence.output_quote: Define a stable base assembly plus selectable modules for features, design elements, child parts and raw materials. Illustrative lamp modules include lighting functions, optical elements, housing/appearance options, electronics and connectors.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Each gate records its owner, evidence, decision, conditions and timestamp. A failed gate returns the case to the relevant step with reasons; conditional decisions cannot authorize release until their conditions are closed.

evidence.source_quote: As a first step, the CPO has asked you to develop the first-level workflow draft for this new sourcing process — both as a strategic process recommendation and as the foundational blueprint for the digital platform the TechSol will build.
evidence.output_quote: Core records: program, part/variant, supplier, TRSO revision, evaluation, module/BOM, quotation revision, negotiation event, nomination baseline, change request, approval and commercial release. Use persistent IDs and explicit links so any price can be traced to its configuration, quote, negotiation and approvals.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable satisfies all functional and audience requirements of the prompt.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are unambiguous and consistent with the operative approval governance design.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
